title: Akshay Rajhans, Ph.D. • 3-й+
text: MathWorks Research Summit is coming to India! After 17 editions of this flagship research and technology conference in Greater Boston and Tokyo, MathWorks is excited to host the inaugural India edition at our Bangalore office on October 27 and 28. The theme of this year's event will be Engineered System Design in the age of AI. What I’m personally most excited about isn’t just bringing the event to India. It’s the opportunity to build and grow a new research community. Many years ago, I started my career as an R&D engineer in India. A lot has changed since then. India’s research and innovation ecosystem has grown tremendously, as has the MathWorks footprint in the country. India has also become an increasingly important part of our research collaborations. The Summit gives us an opportunity to strengthen those existing relationships and build new ones. The goal of the gathering isn’t simply to present work. We want to learn from people across disciplines, have candid conversations about where research is headed, surface challenges that are both global and specific to India, and explore how a common technology platform and ecosystem can help move ideas from exploration to impact. Just as importantly, we hope to create connections that continue well beyond the two days of the Summit. That has been one of the most rewarding outcomes of previous editions, and I’m excited to see what comes from bringing this community together in India. Event registration is free, but by invitation. If you’re interested, you can nominate yourself or a colleague through the nomination form on our Research Summit series page: https://lnkd.in/eGKRTyRu #MathWorksResearchSummit #MathWorks #Research #Engineering #Innovation #India #Academia #MATLAB #Simulink Lakshminarayan Viju Ravichandran , Souvick Chatterjee

title: Emmanuel Schalit
text: OceanWings has secured ClassNK - Nippon Kaiji Kyokai Approval in Principle for its Rigid Fixed and Rigid Tiltable wingsail designs, widening the range of vessel applications that can be assessed for wind-assisted propulsion. The approval builds on a 2025 certification covering a 363m² wingsail with a 38-metre span. OceanWings already offers a 407m² model with a 42-metre span, while the latest approval supports consideration of even larger configurations. “The appropriate dimensions are determined by the technical and operational requirements of each vessel, rather than by a predefined size limitation,” said Emmanuel Schalit , CEO of OceanWings. For shipowners and shipyards, the significance is flexibility: wind propulsion can be assessed earlier against vessel type, deck arrangement and operating profile, whether for newbuilds or retrofits. Read the full story here: https://lnkd.in/een2gwgU #WindPropulsion #Maritime #ClassNK #Decarbonisation #Shipping

title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. • Отслеживаете
text: During a technical review, I asked to see the training data and validation methodology behind a company's "AI-based multi-sensor classifier." What I got back was a fixed decision tree with manually tuned thresholds — no train/test split, no retraining pipeline, a "confidence score" that was really just a normalized distance metric with no calibration behind it. Here's the part people miss: that's not automatically a bad system. A deterministic, explainable rule-based classifier can be exactly the right architectural choice for a safety-critical decision path — arguably safer than a black-box model in a domain where you'll eventually have to explain your logic to a test pilot or an OT&E board. The actual problem was calling it "AI." That label invites the wrong due-diligence questions — where's your training data, how do you retrain, what's your drift monitoring — and forfeits the credit you'd get for being deterministic and auditable in a domain where explainability is a selling point, not a weakness. How you characterize your own architecture changes which questions you get asked. Answer the right ones on your own terms. #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #AI
author: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. • Отслеживаете
